nodes.description: Biallelic CLIC5 variants impair protein function through allele-dependent mechanisms. The Turkish p.Cys32Ter allele predicts early truncation, but nonsense-mediated RNA decay was not confirmed in patient lymphoblastoid cells. The Cameroonian c.63+1G>A donor variant has a predicted, untested splicing effect; p.Leu75Pro shows increased abundance and perinuclear aggregation after ectopic expression in HEK293 cells. These observations do not establish complete absence of protein for every human allele. The Siberian p.Trp215Ter allele is another truncating variant.

nodes.description: The spontaneous C3H/HeJ jitterbug allele deletes 97 genomic bases, causing exon 5 skipping, frameshift and premature termination. Protein is undetectable by the reported assays. Mutants develop hearing and vestibular dysfunction, abnormal stereocilia and later hair-cell degeneration. The 2014 follow-up defines membrane lifting, fusion and altered partner localization. Cochlear supporting structures such as Reissner's membrane and stria vascularis were preserved in the original histology, arguing against a primary endolymph-volume phenotype.

nodes.description:
The gene-replacement study used the ENU-induced nmf318 missense line (JAX 005329), not an engineered knockout. The MGI allele record specifies c.680T>C, p.Phe227Ser; the paper uses Clic5−/− as shorthand for the protein-deficient phenotype. Untreated animals had approximately 40-dB ABR threshold shifts at four weeks and no detected responses at eight weeks.
Left-utricle injection at P0 restored CLIC5, prevented bundle fusion, improved hair-cell survival and auditory/vestibular outcomes. Radixin localization returned toward normal but taperin remained distributed along stereocilia at eight weeks. The self-complementary vector achieved comparable measured benefit at approximately eleven-fold lower titer than the single-stranded construct; this was not a formal equivalence trial, the constructs differed in reporter content and some untreated controls were shared. Auditory benefit declined, especially at high frequencies, whereas vestibular behavioral benefit persisted through the 12-week follow-up. No delayed-treatment arm tested reversal of established damage.

nodes.description:
CLIC5 concentrates near the stereociliary base and adjacent apical membrane. In jitterbug mice, radixin and PTPRQ localization is perturbed before fusion; taperin mislocalization is detected later. Membrane lifting and fusion support impaired attachment to the underlying cytoskeleton, but temporal precedence alone does not prove which interaction initiates the lesion.
Co-immunoprecipitation in epithelial cells and pull-down from mouse lung support association with ERM proteins and taperin, with more tentative evidence for myosin VI. Direct CLIC5-actin binding and the composition of a single native hair-cell complex are not established by these assays. Approximately equimolar CLIC5 and radixin abundance in bulk chicken hair bundles does not establish complex stoichiometry. Myosin VI mutants also mislocalize CLIC5 and radixin, indicating localization dependencies without resolving a unique assembly hierarchy.

nodes.description: Clic5-deficient mice show progressive cochlear and vestibular hair-cell loss after bundle abnormalities. In jitterbug mice, stereocilia were abnormal at P40 without missing hair cells in the imaged preparations, while older animals had severe organ-of-Corti and vestibular degeneration. In the nmf318 AAV study, outer-hair-cell loss was greatest basally, whereas inner-hair-cell survival was largely retained except at the cochlear base. Hearing dysfunction therefore cannot be attributed solely to cell death. P0 gene delivery preceded bundle damage and did not test rescue during the interval between bundle failure and cell loss.

nodes.description: Progressive bilateral sensorineural hearing loss is documented in the reported families. The Turkish siblings progressed from mild loss in early childhood to severe or profound loss before the second decade. Three Cameroonian siblings reported prelingual onset and progression and had profound loss when assessed as adults; earlier audiograms were unavailable. The Siberian cohort ranged from moderate to profound loss and reported highly variable decline, with a mean annual speech-frequency PTA change of 7.4 ± 13.65 dB. This cohort average does not predict an individual trajectory.

nodes.description: CLIC5-deficient hair cells develop membrane lifting, stereocilia fusion and bundle distortion. In the jitterbug deletion line, early bundle abnormalities precede inner-hair-cell fusion at approximately P10; outer-hair-cell fusion becomes prominent after P14 and is more severe basally. In the ENU-induced nmf318 missense model used for AAV therapy, cochlear morphology appeared unchanged at P14 but fusion was present at P17, with inner hair cells affected across regions and outer-hair-cell fusion more severe apically. Utricular bundles were elongated at P15 and thickened by P17. These line- and assay-specific patterns cannot be converted into a human treatment window.
